author: Komorebi P.
new_claims: An actual square polynomial system with a smooth initial lower root has exactly one p-adic root in its prescribed residue ball
Actual integer coefficient perturbation F+cH preserves the lower root and reduced Jacobian at their stated divisibility depths
For a rectangular smooth system, an arbitrary exact root a has a root b of F+cH with b-a divisible by p^M whenever p^M divides c
In the square case M>=L>=1, all selected roots of F and F+cH in the initial ball agree modulo p^M
From a lower square root construct both the original exact root and its uniquely determined nearby perturbed root

scope.coefficients: Finite lists of integer multivariable polynomials; arbitrary p-adic roots
scope.depths: L>=1, M>=L for square stability; M>=1 for rectangular nearby existence
scope.scalar: Any integer c divisible by p^M, including c=0 and negative c
scope.jacobian: Actual DF(x) mod p surjective; d=e only when root uniqueness is asserted
scope.residue_ball: x+p^L Z_p^d; arbitrary roots within that ball, not only a selected tower limit
scope.precision: b-a divisible by p^M; no exact valuation or p^(M+1) claim
scope.dimensions: All finite dimensions allowed by each theorem, including zero

new_modules.note: Support lemmas included; these counts are not counts of independent discoveries.
